questions.question: Nerd Nite has described itself for years with which one-line pitch?
options: TED Talks for the rest of us
It's like the Discovery Channel — with beer!
questions.funFact: The line has stuck because it is honest about both halves. The learning is real and so is the bar tab.

questions.question: A standard Nerd Nite talk is supposed to run how long?
questions.funFact: Long enough to actually teach you something, short enough that nobody's beer goes warm waiting for the conclusion.

questions.question: Chris Balakrishnan started Nerd Nite in a Boston bar in 2003. Which co-founder took it global from New York in 2006 and has been the Big Boss ever since?
questions.funFact: Wasowski and Balakrishnan were college pals. Chris had the idea at the Midway Cafe, Matt turned it into more than 100 cities, and the two later co-wrote a Nerd Nite book together.

talks.title: Don't Fear the Reaper: Tarot & Archetypes
talks.speaker: Hannah Bauer

questions.question: In traditional tarot practice, the Death card is most often read as signifying what?
options: A literal death in the near future
The end of one phase and the start of another
questions.funFact: Readers have taken it this way for centuries, which is why the card turns up far more often in pop culture than in anybody's actual obituary.

questions.question: Carl Jung used the word “shadow” for which part of the psyche?
options: The public personality a person performs for others
Inherited imagery shared across all of humanity
The rational, decision-making centre of the mind
The traits a person represses or refuses to recognise in themselves
questions.funFact: Jung held that the shadow is less evil than unexamined, and that refusing to look at it quietly hands it the steering wheel.

questions.question: The Rider-Waite tarot is the most copied deck in the world. Who actually illustrated all 78 cards?
questions.funFact: Smith painted every card in 1909 for a flat fee and no royalties. The deck carries Waite's name and made his reputation. Hers took most of a century to recover.

talks.title: What the hell is DND anyway?
talks.speaker: Al Marino

questions.question: In Dungeons & Dragons, which die do you roll to find out whether your character succeeds at most things?
questions.funFact: It is so central that the entire underlying rules engine is just called the d20 System.

questions.question: Dungeons & Dragons was first published in 1974. Who co-created it?
questions.funFact: The first run was 1,000 boxed sets, assembled by hand. It sold out inside a year.

questions.question: D&D grew directly out of an earlier tabletop game co-written by Gygax and Jeff Perren. What was that game called?
questions.funFact: Chainmail was a medieval miniatures wargame, and its fantasy supplement added the trolls and dragons. Blackmoor is the trap answer: that was Arneson's campaign setting, not the game itself.
